regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 55.9","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% YoY looks unambiguous — until you note that the RBI's own forecast sits at 6.7% YoY, a 110bps gap that historically reflects deflator assumptions, not real output divergence. PMI Composite at 55.9 and IIP at 8.0% YoY corroborate momentum, but core sector at 4.8% YoY — the eight infrastructure industries that move physical goods — is decelerating. The quality of growth is tilting toward services and financial intermediation; the goods economy is growing, but not accelerating.","badge_label":"Expansion Mode","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 5.54% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"CPI at 5.54% YoY is the headline, but the decomposition is where the problem lives: food at 7.74% YoY is rising for the second consecutive month, fuel at 22.93% YoY is at the 95th percentile historically, and core CPI at 3.9% YoY is the one number the RBI can claim comfort from. The inversion: if core is benign and the RBI cuts on that basis, the second-order effect is that fuel and food inflation — both supply-side and import-driven — feed into rural wage expectations and WPI at 9.92% YoY feeds back into manufactured goods prices within two quarters. The RBI's own inflation forecast of 5.1% YoY already exceeds its 4% target midpoint; a cut here would be a policy error dressed as data-dependence.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 19.4% YoY; CD ratio 81%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 19.4% YoY against deposit growth at 17.8% YoY is a 160bps divergence, and the CD ratio at 81% — 73rd percentile historically — has been falling from 83% but remains structurally elevated. The last time India sustained a CD ratio above 80% while the repo rate was being held was the pre-taper tantrum period of FY13-14; within 12 months, emergency rate action followed. Today's setup differs in one critical respect: NBFC credit is accelerating at 15.8% YoY, services credit at 24.3% YoY, and vehicle credit at 19.7% YoY — the credit expansion is broad-based, not concentrated. That breadth makes macro-prudential tightening via risk weights more likely than a rate move.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. is on extended hold, but the real rate calculus is uncomfortable: with CPI at 5.54% YoY, the real repo rate is effectively negative 29bps. The RBI's inflation forecast of 5.1% YoY implies they expect this to persist. For housing, a 7.35% p.a. average home loan rate against 8% YoY price appreciation in Bengaluru means affordability is not deteriorating further — but any rate hike to defend the INR against FII outflows of ₹49,935 cr / month would reprice mortgages and stall the residential cycle. The RBI is holding a line, not choosing a direction.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.9% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY and capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity — 74th percentile — is the strongest combination in this cycle. The inversion applies here in reverse: at 77.4%, private capex has a credible IRR case; the threshold for crowding-in is typically 75-76%, and India has crossed it. Industry credit at 18.2% YoY confirms that banks are funding this expansion. The risk is that core sector at 4.8% YoY — cement, steel, electricity — is not keeping pace with the capital goods order book, suggesting some of the IIP strength is equipment imports and assembly, not domestic infrastructure throughput.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹203521 cr/mo; PV 7.9% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹2,03,521 cr / month is at the 73rd percentile, but the composition matters: this is a month-on-month uptick from ₹1,99,853 cr / month, not a structural acceleration. Passenger vehicle sales at 7.9% YoY are decelerating — down from 16% and 26.1% in prior months — while two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY are the real signal of rural and mass-market demand recovery. The divergence between PV deceleration and 2W acceleration is the classic India dual-economy tell: urban discretionary is plateauing while rural aspirational is catching up, likely on the back of agricultural credit surging 17.2% YoY.","badge_label":"Stable Consumption","badge_type":"b-neu"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 19.4% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 17.8% YoY — a 160 bps divergence widening for 2 consecutive months (17.1% → 19.4% credit; 9.9% → 17.8% deposits). CD ratio at 81% credit ÷ deposits, down from 82.2% but still at 73rd percentile historically. NBFC credit accelerating at 15.8% YoY (up from 10% YoY), now at 57th percentile. Services credit surging at 24.3% YoY (79th percentile), rising 2 straight months.","implication":"RBI will face pressure to either hike rates to cool credit or inject liquidity to ease deposit stress. Banks with CASA ratios below 40% and wholesale funding > 25% of liabilities face margin compression. Overweight private banks with CASA > 45% (HDFC, ICICI, Axis) — they'll poach deposits. Avoid NBFCs with wholesale funding > 30% of liabilities; their funding costs will spike. Repo rate pause is ending; expect 25-50 bps of tightening by Q2 FY27.","pct_10y":73,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 73rd percentile; last time it was this high (2022), RBI tightened aggressively. Services credit at 79th percentile is a late-cycle signal — demand is strong but funding is strained.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Upcycle Broadens Beyond Capital Goods","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY (52nd percentile), up from 16.1% YoY. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (74th percentile), up from 75.6%. Core sector growth at 4.8% YoY (50th percentile), down from 5% but still stable. India credit to industry at 18.2% YoY (74th percentile), up from 7% YoY. Vehicle credit surging at 19.7% YoY (68th percentile), rising 2 straight months. Agricultural credit at 17.2% YoY (78th percentile), up from 7.6% YoY.","implication":"Capex cycle is broadening from manufacturing into agriculture and commercial vehicles — a sign of genuine demand, not just government spending. Overweight capital goods, auto ancillaries, and construction equipment. Cement and steel demand will remain robust through FY27. Private capex is accelerating; public capex is moderating. Expect 12-15% earnings growth for capex-exposed sectors over next 18 months. Avoid defensive plays; rotation into cyclicals is justified.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 74th percentile is the sweet spot for capex acceleration — not so high that it triggers inflation, not so low that it signals slack. Last time we saw this (2021-22), capex growth sustained for 18+ months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP Inflows Hit 93rd Percentile, But Ticket Size Inflates","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,490 cr / month (93rd percentile), rising 3 straight months (₹29,845 → ₹31,961 → ₹32,297 → ₹32,490 cr / month). SIP accounts at 10.0646 mn (2nd percentile), down from 10.45 mn — a 4% decline. SIP AUM at ₹17.86 lakh cr (89th percentile), up from ₹16.64 lakh cr. Equity MF net inflows at ₹38,307 cr / month (80th percentile), up from ₹29,329 cr / month. DII equity net at ₹51,829 cr / month (95th percentile). NFO collections collapsed to ₹998 cr / month (2nd percentile), down from ₹3,051 cr / month.","implication":"SIP inflows are strong, but account growth is stalling — average ticket size is rising 40% while account count falls 4%. This is affluent money entering, not mass retail. Late-cycle behaviour: high-net-worth individuals are rotating into equities as real estate affordability deteriorates (affordability index at 3.5x, 19th percentile). Domestic institutional flows are masking FII outflows (₹49,935 cr / month net outflow, 17th percentile). Overweight large-cap, dividend-paying stocks; avoid small-cap momentum plays. NFO collapse signals retail fatigue — new product launches will struggle.","pct_10y":93,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 93rd percentile is historically strong, but the divergence between inflow growth (+40% AUM) and account growth (-4%) is a red flag for late-cycle concentration. Last time this happened (2021), retail participation peaked 6 months later.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation at 95th Percentile, Import Bill Swelling","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile), up from 20.05% YoY — a 288 bps jump. Current account deficit will widen; INR depreciation pressure will intensify. Hedge crude exposure; avoid refiners with weak hedging. Overweight renewable energy and EV plays — they're the only way to escape the oil trap.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile is the highest in 3+ years. Last time it was this high (2022), RBI tightened 190 bps in 6 months and INR fell 8%.","is_surprise":false}

signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Collapse Signals GCC Pullback, Not IT Strength","data_text":"Office absorption at 19.5 mn sq ft / quarter (13th percentile), but highly volatile (recent: 4 → 5.3 → 18.7 → 5.3 → 24.6 → 2.6 mn sq ft / quarter). Office vacancy at 14.7% vacant (43rd percentile), up from 14.5% vacant. Nifty IT index flat YTD despite Nifty 50 up 8%. India credit to services at 24.3% YoY (79th percentile), rising 2 straight months — but this is driven by fintech, logistics, and healthcare, NOT IT services. Airline passenger traffic at 86.4 mn / month (35th percentile), up from 85.17 mn / month but still below pre-COVID trend.","implication":"Office absorption is collapsing because Global Capability Centers (GCCs) are consolidating footprints and shifting to flex spaces. Traditional IT services (TCS, Infosys, Wipro) are NOT the driver of office demand anymore. Services credit growth is real, but it's fintech (CRED, Razorpay, Stripe India), logistics (Delhivery, Ecom Express), and healthcare (Apollo, Fortis), not IT. This means: (1) Overweight fintech and logistics; underweight legacy IT services. (2) Commercial real estate (Embassy, Mindspace, Brookfield REITs) are facing structural headwinds — GCC consolidation will persist. (3) Airline traffic at 35th percentile suggests business travel is NOT recovering — another sign that IT services are in secular decline. Falsifiable: If IT services credit growth exceeds 15% YoY in next 2 months, this thesis breaks.","pct_10y":13,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 13th percentile is the lowest in the dataset. The divergence between services credit growth (79th percentile) and office absorption (13th percentile) is the key insight — services are growing, but NOT in traditional IT office space. This is a structural shift from IT services to fintech/logistics/healthcare.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

7.8% GDP, But the Goods Economy Is Losing Altitude

The facts:

  • India GDP at 7.8% YoY (64th percentile) — the RBI's own forecast is 6.7% YoY, a 110bps gap that implies statistical discrepancy, not consensus.
  • PMI Composite at 55.9 (85th percentile) and IIP at 8.0% YoY confirm services and manufacturing momentum.
  • But core sector at 4.8% YoY (50th percentile) is decelerating — the eight infrastructure industries that proxy physical goods movement are not keeping pace.
  • Two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY signal rural demand recovery; passenger vehicle sales at 7.9% YoY are falling for the second consecutive month — the economy's two halves are diverging.

The tension: Headline GDP and PMI signal broad expansion; core sector deceleration and PV sales slowdown suggest the goods economy is plateauing while services carry the aggregate number.

Bottom line: Watch core sector YoY: a print below 4.0% YoY would confirm goods-economy stall and challenge the GDP-PMI consensus.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

DM Equity Euphoria Meets Bond Market Reality

The facts:

  • Euro Stoxx 50 at 6,116 (100th percentile) and S&P 500 at 7,677 (100th percentile) — both at 10-year highs, pricing re-acceleration.
  • But US 10Y Treasury at 5.0% yield (90th percentile) is doing the Fed's tightening work; US GDP SAAR at 2.2% SAAR is decelerating from 2.5% SAAR.
  • BOJ rate at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile), rising for the second consecutive month — yen carry unwind is not a tail risk, it is in progress.
  • Global PMI Composite at 54.3 (84th percentile) and US PMI at 58.4 (91st percentile) — survey data and bond markets are telling opposite stories.

The tension: Equity markets are pricing a growth re-acceleration that nominal GDP data does not support; bond markets at 5.0% yield are pricing persistent tightening that equity multiples have not absorbed.

Bottom line: BOJ at 1.25% p.a. is the underpriced tail: each 25bps hike unwinds carry trades that have funded EM equity inflows, including India's DII buffer.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

SIP Autopilot Holds, But Institutional Conviction Has Thinned

The facts:

  • SIP inflows at ₹32,490 cr / month (93rd percentile), rising for three consecutive months — retail allocation is systematic, not sentiment-driven.
  • But SIP accounts at 10.06 mn (2nd percentile), down from 10.45 mn — fewer accounts generating higher inflows means ticket size is inflating, not participation broadening.
  • DII equity net at ₹51,829 cr / month (95th percentile) absorbing FII equity outflows of ₹49,935 cr / month (17th percentile) — the offset is near-perfect but fragile.
  • NFO collections at ₹998 cr / month (2nd percentile), down from ₹3,051 cr / month — fund houses are not launching because institutional demand for new product is absent.

The tension: Retail SIP flows are mechanically strong, but the market is being held up by a shrinking base of high-ticket investors; any SIP slowdown removes the only structural buyer absorbing FII exits.

Bottom line: Watch SIP account count: a further decline below 9.8 mn would signal retail participation is narrowing, not deepening — the DII buffer becomes less reliable.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

India VIX Rising Into Equity Highs — REITs Price the Office Risk

The facts:

  • NRI buying is RISING — NRI share of residential purchases at 18% (up 8 pp), with 25% share within premium/luxury; Bengaluru, Mumbai, and Hyderabad are the primary destinations.
  • Hyderabad leads city momentum: sales +15% YoY, launches +120% YoY, but unsold inventory at 28 months — the launch surge is running ahead of absorption.
  • India VIX at 17.16 (13th percentile historically, but rising for four of the last five sessions) while Nifty 50 at 22,753 — volatility is cheap relative to the macro risk stack.
  • But Embassy REIT at ₹370/unit, Mindspace at ₹345/unit, Brookfield at ₹263/unit — all down sharply from prior levels, pricing office absorption risk that GCC occupancy data (42% of leasing) does not yet justify.

The tension: NRI demand and DII flows are supporting residential and equity prices; REIT valuations are diverging downward as office absorption volatility (ranging 2.6–24.6 mn sq ft / quarter) makes income visibility impossible to price.

Bottom line: REITs are a buy only if Q4 office absorption exceeds 20 mn sq ft / quarter — below that, the yield case collapses against a 5.0% US 10Y.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Three Fuses, One Detonator — Fuel, Carry, and Credit

The facts:

  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) — Brent at $110/bbl means every $10 move adds ~$15bn to India's annual import bill and widens CAD by ~40bps; INR at 95.24 has no buffer.
  • BOJ at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile) — carry unwind risk is live; FII equity outflows already at ₹49,935 cr / month, and DII absorption at 95th percentile cannot sustain indefinitely.
  • Bank credit at 19.4% YoY vs deposits at 17.8% YoY — if the 160bps divergence widens further, RBI macro-prudential action on risk weights is the most probable policy response, not a rate cut.
  • US CPI at 3.72% YoY, rising for three consecutive months — a Fed re-acceleration scenario would push US 10Y above 5.25% yield and reprice all EM risk assets simultaneously.

The tension: Each risk is individually manageable; the scenario where Brent holds above $110/bbl, BOJ hikes again, and the Fed delays cuts simultaneously is not priced — India's $680bn reserve buffer buys months, not quarters.

Bottom line: Watch Brent crude this week: a close above $115/bbl triggers the CAD-INR-inflation feedback loop that forces the RBI's hand before the next MPC meeting.

"}
